audience_problem: A beginner may mistake an initial task payment or an app balance for proof that an online job is real.

hook.text: An online job pays you a little, then says: deposit money to unlock your earnings

payoff.text: The F T C warns that task scams can show fake app balances and use early payments to build trust.

packaging.title: This 'Online Job' Asks You to Pay First — Stop
packaging.promise: Show the pay-to-unlock task-scam pattern and give the concrete boundary: do not deposit money.
packaging.evidence_anchor: The F T C warns that task scams can show fake app balances and use early payments to build trust.

sources.claim: Task scammers may build trust with a small payment, display fake app earnings, then demand personal deposits to unlock tasks or withdrawals.
Unsolicited fake-recruiter texts can seek engagement before asking for money. The FTC advises ignoring generic unexpected job messages and not paying to get paid.
